scope: High-priority evidence for environment risk review, magnesium nutrition, nutrient trend/control records, and Cannabis genome interpretation.
rules: Controlled Cannabis environmental and nutrient studies remain bounded to tested genotype, stage, media and environmental conditions.
Response-surface optima are experimental model outputs, not universal fertilizer recipes.
Visual nutrient symptoms are nonspecific and require measured system context.
Genome coordinates, associations and annotations must name the reference/assay context; variants are not complete phenotype predictions.
All mappings remain pending independent science review.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Controlled Cannabis humidity experiments show that environmental humidity can alter flowering development and measured cannabinoid outcomes, while greenhouse VPD literature shows that useful microclimate ranges remain crop- and system-dependent rather than universal.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Corredor-Perilla et al. (2025), DOI 10.3389/fpls.2025.1678142; Shamshiri et al. (2018), DOI 10.1515/intag-2017-0005.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports building environmental control envelopes from stage, measured crop response, tissue/environment measurements and facility capability instead of copying one chart.
claimEvidence.limitations: The Cannabis study's treatment effects are specific to its germplasm and conditions; neither source establishes a universal temperature-RH-VPD schedule.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Vegetative medical-Cannabis responses to magnesium supply include measurable physiological, mineral and visual changes, supporting magnesium's nutritional role while showing that supply-response interpretation requires stage and system context.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Morad and Bernstein (2023), PMID 37514248, PMCID PMC10384070, DOI 10.3390/plants12142676.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports measured magnesium diagnosis and correction while separating physiological evidence from symptom-only diagnosis.
claimEvidence.limitations: The experiment is vegetative-stage and genotype/system specific. Its treatment concentrations and response optimum are not universal Cannabis feed targets, and interveinal chlorosis is not uniquely diagnostic of Mg deficiency.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Multifactor Cannabis nutrient experiments can model interacting N-P-K responses and identify treatment-specific response surfaces, illustrating why nutrient decisions should retain treatment composition, response measurements and model context rather than reducing records to a single EC value.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Bevan, Jones, and Zheng (2021), PMID 34868115, PMCID PMC8638000, DOI 10.3389/fpls.2021.764103.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports controlled nutrient records, trend review and traceable corrective-action reasoning using measured variables and explicit experimental/system context.
claimEvidence.limitations: Response-surface model optima are bounded to the studied cultivar, flowering stage, soilless system and environmental conditions; production correlations do not by themselves prove causation.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Cannabis genome assemblies and population comparisons provide reference coordinates and evidence of genomic variation/introgression, but assembly choice, ancestry and structural variation affect interpretation and a detected allele or locus is not a complete prediction of crop phenotype.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the lesson's DNA/gene/allele/chromosome hierarchy and requirement to record reference build and assay limitations when interpreting variants.
claimEvidence.limitations: Genome associations and coordinates are reference- and germplasm-dependent; the study does not establish deterministic phenotype prediction for arbitrary Cannabis lines.
